thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall — streaming-inference p99 latency breach detected in us-west-2 (service=streaming-inference). p99 is 1.88s (SLO=1.2s) and we've seen a spike in streaming stalls. Auto-evacuate attempted for node gpu-12 but some sessions remained attached. Tagging oncall.

sam-w: acked. oncall taking. I'm pulling dashboards now.

marta-eng: thanks. any customer-facing errors reported?

prod-support: getting a couple of slow complaints from a customer in finance-dev this morning, sessions hung ~5-8s before eventual completion. low volume but a noticeable tail.

ben-sre: looking at node telemetry — gpu-12 shows rising correctable ECC counts and repeated thermal throttle events in the last 15m. nvml shows ECC correctables++ and temperature spikes to ~89C.

sam-w: can you paste the `nvidia-smi`/dmesg snippets?

ben-sre: sure — snippet: ```
Timestamp: 2026-03-15T15:18:23Z
GPU 12: ECC corrected errors: 124 -> 137
GPU 12: GPU_TEMP: 89C (throttling engaged)
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 45, PID 2345, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

kevin-ml: that matches the KV cache stall traces—some streaming requests saw repeated KV miss + reattach which inflates tail latency.

sam-w: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon+drain gpu-12 (evacuate active sessions) 2) fallback routing to model-v1-small for streaming route to reduce per-token GPU load 3) temporarily reduce batching to keep latency down 4) notify customers if we expect >5m impact. agree?

marta-eng: +1. also enable region fallback to us-west-1 for new sessions to reduce stress on us-west-2 while we evict. do we have capacity? opsbot, can you confirm spare headroom?

opsbot: spare headroom check: us-west-2 free GPUs: 6 (after reserved), estimated available qps headroom ~18% for streaming workloads. can autoscale up additional nodes in 2m if needed.

ben-sre: draining now: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-12 && kubectl drain node/gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`. starting graceful eviction; might take up to 90s for long-lived streams.

incident-bot: action logged: `drain initiated` by ben-sre at 1860012380.

sam-w: while drain completes, toggle routing: `routing-policy streaming-inference/us-west-2 -> prefer model-v1-small, fallback region us-west-1`. Also reduce max batch size from 8 -> 4 on streaming queue.

kevin-ml: quick check on quality: v1-small reduces latency but increases token count ~+3% on some prompts. we'll monitor regressions on the eval set.

prod-support: drafting customer note — short blurb: "We detected transient latency spikes for streaming responses in us-west-2 due to a degraded accelerator node. We have routed new sessions away and are mitigating — customers may see slightly longer responses for a subset of streaming calls. We'll update when fully resolved." 

marta-eng: good. set expectation: update in 15m or on next significant event.

ben-sre: drain complete, node cordoned, GPU driver logs show persistent ECC correctables + thermal entries. marking node hardware-failed for replacement. moving workloads off.

incident-bot: mitigation status: routing policy updated, node gpu-12 isolated, autoscale emergency policy not triggered. p99 dropped to 1.25s in last 2m (monitoring).

sam-w: monitoring trend — p95 back to 0.55s, p99 at 1.25s (still slightly above SLO). continue to monitor for 30m, but immediate customer impact appears contained.

ben-sre: creating follow-up ticket to replace GPU card and run extended bake tests on node. will attach logs: ECC counts, thermal history, driver Xids.

marta-eng: runbook notes: add step to force immediate routing cutover when heavy ECC correctables >100 in 10m. also add checklist for model fallback QoS detection.

prod-support: sending initial customer message now. will update when we confirm full recovery.

kevin-ml: will run a quick eval to measure any short-term quality drift from v1-small fallback and report.

sam-w: handing off monitoring and next steps to ben-sre for hardware remediation and to marta-eng for routing/runbook follow-up. I'm going offline for the next handoff. thanks team. :thumbsup:
